title: Using Sandbox Integration with Zero Trust Browser

blocks.text: For organizations using both Internet & SaaS (ZIA) Sandbox and Zero Trust Browser (formerly Isolation), an integration between these modules exists which provides additional benefits, maximizing both security and end-user productivity. To learn more, see About Sandbox and About Sandbox Integration with Zero Trust Browser.

When a user opens an unknown file, such as a PDF or Microsoft Office document, the file initially opens in the isolated browser. This isolated environment prevents any malicious content from reaching the user's endpoint, but still allows them to access the original file to maximize user productivity, while Sandbox is analyzing the file. You can identify the file's status by the Zero Trust Browser URL and the Sandbox banner.

blocks.item: Configure the Sandbox policy in Internet & SaaS. To learn more, see Configuring the Sandbox Policy.
In your isolation profile, enable the Sandbox option for file transfer. To learn more, see Creating Isolation Profiles for Internet & SaaS.

blocks.text: To use Sandbox with Zero Trust Browser:

blocks.item: Download a file that triggers a Sandbox policy. An isolated browser window opens to render the file.

When rendering is complete, Sandbox scans the rendered file and determines whether it contains malicious content. If it does, a red Sandbox banner appears. If it does not, a blue Sandbox banner appears.

If the file is malicious, click the red Sandbox banner and select your download option: the Original File or a Flattened PDF. Downloading a flattened PDF gives you the option to view the file with the malicious content removed.
If the content is benign, click the blue Sandbox banner to download the original file.
Depending on your choice, the downloaded file is saved to your local device.
